pickRows.seasonSummary: 2025-26 Season: 17-655th Place, Southeast DivisionDid not qualify for playoffs
pickRows.preDraftOutlook: After installing new management a year ago, the Wizards went about shuffling the deck in preparation for a reinvention. It’s safe to say that all has gone well. The club made midseason deals to add accomplished veterans in Anthony Davis and Trae Young to a young developmental core. And now the incoming piece from the draft very well could be the building block this franchise has long desired. It’s a new day in D.C.
pickRows.wayToGo: This draft doesn’t feature a singular, transformational talent like a Victor Wembanyama, but at least two come close enough. And of those, AJ Dybantsa has the size and athletic ability to push him past Darryn Peterson. That’s the safe (and, perhaps,) smart choice for the Wizards, who need to nail this decision for the sake of the future. Dybantsa has the look of greatness and just as important, high entertainment value. — Shaun Powell
pickRows.localTeamNotes: Top-pick team can prioritize ceiling over narrow positional fit. Official NBA.com order pick 1. Need signal: fit_signal_supported; confidence low_medium; usable explicit tags.

pickRows.seasonSummary: 2025-26 Season: 22-605th place, Northwest DivisionDid not qualify for playoffs
pickRows.preDraftOutlook: For a team that won 17 games in 2024-25 and 22 games in 2025-26, scoring and depth are necessities. Utah has building blocks with veterans and young players, and next season, the Jazz should be in a position to begin showing more progress.
pickRows.wayToGo: The Jazz haven’t had a top-two pick since drafting Darrell Griffith second in the 1980 draft. Selecting Kansas guard Darryn Peterson is the kind of scorer and shooter who should accelerate Utah’s rebuild. — Jeff Zillgitt
pickRows.localTeamNotes: Needs a lead initiator who can organize young frontcourt pieces. Official NBA.com order pick 2. Need signal: explicit_need_supported; confidence medium; usable explicit tags.

pickRows.seasonSummary: 2025-26 Season: 25-575th Place, Southwest DivisionDid not qualify for playoffs
pickRows.preDraftOutlook: An injury-plagued 2025-26 sent the Grizzlies back down in their recent up-and-down cycle, and this valley might stick if trading Ja Morant comes to fruition. Memphis used 33 different players last season, ranking toward the bottom of both offensive and defensive rankings. Only Cam Spencer (72), Jaylen Wells (69) and Cedric Coward (62) participated in more than 55 games. Morant appeared in just 20, which puts his value at a low point, should Memphis move him.
pickRows.wayToGo: The first tier of draft elites is four deep, and most mocks pencil in Duke forward Cameron Boozer at No. 3 for the Grizzlies. His fit would be natural alongside center Zach Edey, Wells and Coward, with some NBA pedigree and laudable character traits. At No. 16, Texas Tech guard Christian Anderson could be plugged into Morant’s spot if Memphis deals him — or could play alongside him if he stays. Other backcourt possibilities include Stanford’s Ebuka Okorie and Iowa’s Bennett Stirtz. — Steve Aschburner
pickRows.localTeamNotes: Best value is a high-floor frontcourt hub who can help quickly. Official NBA.com order pick 3. Need signal: multiple_pick_mixed_signal; confidence low_medium; needs review.

pickRows.seasonSummary: 2025-26 Season: 31-514th place, Central DivisionDid not qualify for playoffs
pickRows.preDraftOutlook: The resilience, hope, stubbornness, or gullibility of Chicago Bulls fans should never be underestimated when it comes to offseason makeovers. Another disappointing, aimless season finally led to the dismissal of executive VP of basketball operations Arturas Karnisovas and GM Marc Eversley. As much as ownership favored coach Billy Donovan, he resigned and was replaced by former Blazers interim coach Tiago Splitter in June. The Bulls’ streak of three Play-In appearances ended, too. All it took for Chicago to perk up, though, was popping fourth in the draft lottery. The Bulls have another first-round pick, too, fortunate because their talent cupboard is pretty bare.
pickRows.wayToGo: New basketball boss Bryson Graham will oversee an almost-complete rebuild. He has picks and cap space to fill the roster to match his vision. Chicago is the only team with two picks in the first 15 picks and the No. 4 selection is the obvious prize, with Caleb Wilson or Cameron Boozer slotted in at that spot in many mock drafts. Perimeter shooting and more frontline help are itches to scratch with their remaining picks. — Steve Aschburner
pickRows.localTeamNotes: Roster needs size and creation more than another low-usage guard. Official NBA.com order pick 4. Need signal: explicit_need_supported; confidence medium; usable explicit tags.

pickRows.seasonSummary: 2025-26 Season: 42-403rd place, Pacific DivisionLost in SoFi Play-In Tournament
pickRows.preDraftOutlook: After pulling off one of the greatest in-season turnarounds in NBA history — overcoming a 6-21 start to finish above .500 at 42-40 — the Clippers’ good fortune ran out in the postseason as they were eliminated in the SoFi NBA Play-In Tournament. Then came the NBA Draft Lottery, where the Clippers emerged as one of the biggest winners of the night. With Indiana falling out of the top four, the Clippers acquired their pick (No. 5 overall) as part of the trade that sent Ivica Zubac from LA to Indiana earlier this year.
pickRows.wayToGo: With the 2026 Draft class bursting with top-tier potential — even beyond the consensus top four of AJ Dybantsa, Darryn Peterson, Cam Boozer, and Caleb Wilson — the Clippers are in a great position to bolster their roster with a potential star. If they look to add a guard to slot in next to Darius Garland, keep an eye on prospects like Brayden Burries, Keaton Wagler and Darius Acuff Jr. — _Brian Martin_
pickRows.localTeamNotes: Traded pick context makes upside and trade value important. Official NBA.com order pick 5, acquired from Indiana. Need signal: explicit_fit_and_asset_signal_supported; confidence medium; usable explicit tags.

pickRows.seasonSummary: 2025-26 Season: 20-625th Place, Atlantic DivisionDid not qualify for playoffs
pickRows.preDraftOutlook: A third straight season with at least 50 losses led to a second straight disappointing result in the 2026 Draft Lottery. The Nets didn’t necessarily strike out in last year’s draft, but none of the five players they selected in the first round was an All-Rookie candidate or a clear future starter on a playoff team. There are some useful veterans on this roster, but no franchise cornerstone.
pickRows.wayToGo: It seems doubtful, but if there’s any way the Nets can trade into the top four of the Draft, they should go for it, because they need to find a player with the highest ceiling possible. If they remain at six, they’re probably looking at a group of freshmen guards that includes Darius Acuff Jr., Mikel Brown Jr., Brayden Burries and Keaton Wagler. The Nets can also use their cap space for more high-ceiling shopping and asset collection. — John Schuhmann
pickRows.localTeamNotes: Can take a creator with development runway. Official NBA.com order pick 6. Need signal: mixed_signal_needs_review; confidence low; needs review.

pickRows.seasonSummary: 2025-26 Season: 22-605th place, Pacific DivisionDid not qualify for playoffs
pickRows.preDraftOutlook: With three starters each missing more than half the season — Zach LaVine (39 games played), Domantas Sabonis (19) and Keegan Murray (23) — the Kings posted their lowest win total in 14 years and headed to the Draft Lottery for the 19th time in 20 seasons. Despite entering tied for the fourth-best odds (11.5%) of landing the top pick, the Kings fell all the way to seventh. With the No. 7 pick and a pair of second-round selections, they’ll look for another young building block to pair with last year’s promising rookie trio of Nique Clifford, Maxime Raynaud and Dylan Cardwell.
pickRows.localTeamNotes: Best fit is a guard who creates easy offense without killing tempo. Official NBA.com order pick 7. Need signal: explicit_need_supported; confidence medium; usable explicit tags.

pickRows.seasonSummary: 2025-26 Season: 46-361st Place, Southeast DivisionLost in first round
pickRows.preDraftOutlook: The Hawks are coming off a solid year with a mostly young core which means they’re right on their timeline. Normally they’d be in the market for trading one of their first-round picks for veteran help, but the draft is deep enough that it makes sense to add more youth. The No. 8 pick was famously obtained from the Pelicans on last year’s draft day just to move down a few spots.
pickRows.wayToGo: The Hawks need size but the depth at guard in the top part of the draft might be too enticing to ignore. With the uncertainty about free agent CJ McCollum, the Hawks could opt to find his replacement. A good choice is Mikel Brown from Louisville, whose best talent might lie with his passing, which would ease that burden from Jalen Johnson. The Hawks also have an additional first-rounder and that’s where a big man could fall, such as Tarris Reed from Connecticut, who’s 6-foot-11 yet raw. — Shaun Powell
pickRows.localTeamNotes: Pick acquired from another team gives room for a specialized big. Official NBA.com order pick 8, acquired from New Orleans. Need signal: mixed_signal_needs_review; confidence low; needs review.

pickRows.seasonSummary: 2025-26 Season: 26-565th Place, Southwest DivisionDid not qualify for playoffs
pickRows.preDraftOutlook: In the last 16 months, the Mavs have traded a perennial Kia MVP candidate (Luka Dončić), drafted one of the most heralded prospects in recent memory, traded the future Hall of Famer (Anthony Davis) they got for the first guy, and made major changes in the front office. Cooper Flagg is obviously the foundation, but most of the supporting cast is much older than the Kia Rookie of the Year. That cast includes Kyrie Irving, who should be ready to return at the start of next season, and a new coach after Jason Kidd is out after five seasons.
pickRows.wayToGo: The Mavs fell a spot in the Lottery, but (because of trades) this still could be the highest they pick in the next few years. Flagg is a downhill attacker, so they should be complementing him with as much shooting as they can find. Brayden Burries shot 39% from deep at Arizona, but the Mavs may prefer the potential of Mikel Brown Jr. or the size of Nate Ament. — John Schuhmann
pickRows.localTeamNotes: Contending context favors a cleaner role and shooting translation. Official NBA.com order pick 9. Need signal: mixed_signal_needs_review; confidence low; needs review.

pickRows.seasonSummary: 2025-26 Season: 32-503rd Place, Central DivisionDid not qualify for playoffs
pickRows.preDraftOutlook: Everything Bucks-related at this stage hangs on the potential trade of superstar Giannis Antetokounmpo. All signs point to him playing his 13th NBA season for another franchise, and if that happens, it seals Milwaukee’s approach to 2026-27 and beyond as a down-to-the-studs rebuild. The roster is threadbare and coach Doc Rivers is gone, having snagged his alleged dream job a couple of seasons too late. Rivers’ replacement, Taylor Jenkins, can fit whether he has Antetokounmpo on board or not.
pickRows.wayToGo: The Athletic reported that the Bucks met and spoke with a fleet of draft prospects at the Chicago combine, enough that the tactic seemed to extend beyond just the No. 10 pick. It could have been prep work for securing multiple picks in an 11th-hour Antetokounmpo transaction, a way to kick-start the rebuilding process in a draft regarded as deep. One player’s name has appeared in multiple mocks: Tennessee’s Nate Ament. The 6-foot-10 wing could help with or without Antetokounmpo and showed enough between a slow start and a late-season injury to merit consideration here. Another name: Alabama guard Labaron Philon Jr. to team in the backcourt with Ryan Rollins, one of Milwaukee’s few bright spots from last season. — Steve Aschburner
pickRows.localTeamNotes: Immediate role fit matters more than a long development arc. Official NBA.com order pick 10. Need signal: explicit_need_supported; confidence medium; usable explicit tags.

pickRows.seasonSummary: 2025-26 Season: 37-454th place, Pacific DivisionLost in SoFi Play-In Tournament
pickRows.preDraftOutlook: Following their third straight appearance in the SoFi NBA Play-In Tournament — a stretch where the Warriors made a run to the conference semifinals in 2025 but missed the playoffs in 2024 and 2026 — the Warriors announced a new two-year deal for head coach Steve Kerr. The extension is a clear indication that Golden State remains in win-now mode around Steph Curry and Draymond Green, rather than looking toward the future. However, the front office enters the offseason facing a slew of potential free agents while two key rotation players — Jimmy Butler III (ACL) and Moses Moody (patella) — are currently dealing with long-term knee injuries.
pickRows.wayToGo: The Warriors hold a lottery pick, No. 11 overall, for the first time since 2021. That year, they selected Jonathan Kuminga (No. 7) and Moody (No. 14), following the 2020 selection of James Wiseman (No. 2). Those picks represented the franchise’s ill-fated “two timelines” strategy — an attempt to develop elite young talent for the future while remaining a perennial title contender. Now, in 2026, the trio of Curry, Green, and Butler III (assuming a midseason return) are all in their mid-to-late 30s. That raises the question of whether Golden State should use the 11th pick on a young prospect or package it for an established veteran. If the Warriors keep the pick, keep an eye on Yaxel Lendeborg. The 6-foot-9 forward helped lead Michigan to the NCAA title and will turn 24 by the time his rookie NBA season begins. — Brian Martin
pickRows.localTeamNotes: System fit rewards processing, shooting and low-mistake play. Official NBA.com order pick 11. Need signal: fit_signal_needs_review; confidence low; needs review.

pickRows.preDraftOutlook: The Thunder are in an enviable position given all the talent on the roster, and the front office led by Sam Presti will look to add more talent especially if keeping the current roster becomes problematic financially under salary cap rules. The Thunder prioritize defensive wings, players who can thrive in their player development program and big men who can protect the rim.
pickRows.localTeamNotes: Deep roster can swing on a developmental or positional luxury pick. Official NBA.com order pick 12, acquired from LA Clippers. Need signal: asset_and_fit_signal_needs_review; confidence low; needs review.

pickRows.seasonSummary: 2025-26 Season: 43-394th Place, Southeast DivisionLost in SoFi Play-In Tournament
pickRows.preDraftOutlook: Miami will enter the offseason on the hunt for a superstar — that’s the Pat Riley way. And this franchise hasn’t had one since the breakup of the Big 3, with all due respect to Bam Adebayo. That said, the Heat own a good pick in a deep draft, and perhaps their superstar search will fetch a future foundational piece in the first round.
pickRows.wayToGo: Miami could use depth at guard, a position that will be plentiful even at the No. 13 pick. For example, if Labaron Philon Jr. is around, the Heat would likely not resist. He averaged 22 points at Alabama last year. It’s really about how the first dozen picks impact Miami’s decision-making, because at that spot, there’s the likely chance of a higher-ranking player falling to Miami. — Shaun Powell
pickRows.localTeamNotes: Profile should survive demanding defensive and conditioning standards. Official NBA.com order pick 13. Need signal: explicit_need_supported; confidence medium; usable explicit tags.

pickRows.seasonSummary: 2025-26 Season: 44-383rd Place, Southeast DivisionLost in SoFi Play-In Tournament
pickRows.preDraftOutlook: This team was built organically; the Hornets’ top four players — Brandon Miller, LaMelo Ball, Kon Knueppel and Miles Bridges — were obtained through the draft (Bridges in a draft-day trade with the Clippers). And lo and behold, the Hornets have a pair of picks in the top 20. Given that this is a deep draft and that they’ve been rather smart with their draft selections in the past, the Hornets are in a great position to nab another rotational player or two and let the youngsters keep growing together.
pickRows.wayToGo: The Hornets are marginal at one position — big man. There’s an urgency to spend one of the picks on size, and there should be solid candidates around, notably Hannes Steinbach (6-foot-11) from Washington if Aday Mara (7-foot-3) of Michigan is off the board. Also, with the other pick, 19-year-old wing Karim López comes from the same Australian grooming ground as LaMelo. — Shaun Powell
pickRows.localTeamNotes: Young core benefits from a reliable interior complement. Official NBA.com order pick 14. Need signal: explicit_need_with_trade_uncertainty; confidence medium; needs review.

pickRows.seasonSummary: 2025-26 Season: 46-363rd Place, Atlantic DivisionLost in first round
pickRows.preDraftOutlook: The Raptors were one of the league’s most improved teams this season, adding 16 wins to go from the Lottery to the East’s No. 5 seed. They lost in the first round of the playoffs, but Scottie Barnes (25 years old in August) and Collin Murray-Boyles (21) established themselves as franchise cornerstones.
pickRows.wayToGo: The Raptors need shooting and playmaking, whether they come via trade, free agency or the Draft. But both Barnes and Murray-Boyles are malleable enough that they should be looking to pick the best player available at 19. Christian Anderson and Cameron Carr would give them some much-needed shooting if either is available, but they could also look at potential, long-term replacements for Jakob Poeltl like Chris Cenac Jr., Morez Johnson Jr. or Hannes Steinbach. — John Schuhmann
pickRows.localTeamNotes: Length and multi-position defense remain the cleanest identity fit. Official NBA.com order pick 19. Need signal: explicit_need_supported; confidence medium; usable explicit tags.

pickRows.seasonSummary: 2025-26 Season: 62-201st Place, Southwest DivisionLost in NBA Finals
pickRows.preDraftOutlook: The Spurs are a modern-day model of team building through the draft, and it helps to be both good at scouting and lucky in the lottery. With the exception of De’Aaron Fox, the top players in the rotation are home grown. Once again, the Spurs — thanks to the Atlanta Hawks — own a top-20 pick, and even though they’re a contending team and should be for years to come with Victor Wembanyama, another highly-regarded young player certainly can’t hurt.
pickRows.wayToGo: Because of their lofty place in the NBA power pecking order, the Spurs don’t need immediate help. In that sense, it would seem wise for them to take a chance on Jayden Quaintance, the 6-foot-10 forward who only played four games last season for Kentucky while dealing with knee surgery. They can put him in their very respected player development program and watch him grow without any pressure or urgency; he’s just 18 years old. — Shaun Powell
pickRows.localTeamNotes: Needs a guard who complements high-usage frontcourt creation. Official NBA.com order pick 20, acquired from Atlanta. Need signal: explicit_need_supported; confidence medium; usable explicit tags.

pickRows.seasonSummary: 2025-26 Season: 60-221st Place, Central DivisionLost in conference semifinals
pickRows.preDraftOutlook: A marvelous season for Detroit ended with a thud in Game 7 of their Eastern Conference semifinals vs. Cleveland. So much until then had been impressive: Winning 60 games, claiming the East’s No. 1 seed, riding guard Cade Cunningham to Kia MVP contender status, Jalen Duren’s rise to All-Star and All-NBA acclaim, and even bouncing back against Orlando from a 3-1 deficit in the first round. Getting eliminated by the Cavs stung, and the abrupt end of the Pistons’ postseason highlighted some holes to plug, primarily additional scoring and backcourt for Cunningham.
pickRows.wayToGo: Most of the Pistons’ progress will come from within with the young players such as Duren, Ausar Thompson, and Isaiah Stewart positioned for contract extensions. But the No. 21 pick they got is a legit asset in this deep prospect pool. Duke’s Isaiah Evans could be helpful as a Cunningham sidekick and points source, with shooting range to open up the floor. Three other possibilities: Iowa point guard Bennett Stirtz, Texas Tech guard Christian Anderson and Texas wing Dailyn Swain. — Steve Aschburner
pickRows.localTeamNotes: Role clarity matters around existing young ball handlers. Official NBA.com order pick 21, acquired from Minnesota. Need signal: explicit_need_supported; confidence medium; usable explicit tags.

pickRows.seasonSummary: 2025-26 Season: 45-374th Place, Atlantic DivisionLost in conference semifinals
pickRows.preDraftOutlook: In VJ Edgecombe and Tyrese Maxey, the Sixers have two star guards who are 20 and 25 years old, respectively. They also have two former Kia MVP candidates — Joel Embiid and Paul George — on the other side of 30. Both have missed many games over the last two years _and_ are owed more than $230 million over the next two years. The Sixers also have a new front office: they fired team president Daryl Morey and replaced him with Mike Gansey shortly after the team was swept in the Eastern Conference semifinals.
pickRows.wayToGo: Embiid and George probably aren’t going anywhere, but the Gansey-led front office should be all-in on the Maxey-and-Edgecombe timeline. There should be some complementary bigs and big wings to choose from with the No. 22 pick, including Chris Cenac Jr., Isaiah Evans, Allen Graves and Morez Johnson Jr.. — John Schuhmann
pickRows.localTeamNotes: Pick should produce a rotation pathway quickly. Official NBA.com order pick 22, acquired from Houston via Oklahoma City. Need signal: explicit_need_supported; confidence medium; usable explicit tags.

pickRows.seasonSummary: 2025-26 Season: 53-292nd Place, Atlantic Division2026 NBA Champions
pickRows.preDraftOutlook: The Knicks had some ups and downs in the regular season, but were dominant through the playoffs, going 16-3 through all four rounds to win the team’s first NBA title in 53 years. Their starting lineup remains under contract and they’re built to win now.
pickRows.wayToGo: While the starters are all under contract, the Knicks’ reserves are mostly free agents. With this being a win-now situation, they should be looking for players that can contribute right away with the 24th and 31st picks, when upperclassmen Joshua Jefferson, Alex Karaban, Bennett Stirtz, Dailyn Swain and Henri Veesaar could be available. — John Schuhmann
pickRows.localTeamNotes: Late first should fit a playoff rotation role. Official NBA.com order pick 24. Need signal: explicit_need_supported; confidence medium; usable explicit tags.

pickRows.seasonSummary: 2025-26 Season: 53-291st place, Pacific DivisionLost in conference semifinals
pickRows.preDraftOutlook: The Lakers posted back-to-back 50-win seasons for the first time in 15 years, but their 2026 playoff run was doomed by an injury to Luka Dončić and a West Semis matchup with OKC that ended in a sweep. L.A. enters the offseason with only two of its top 10 scorers under contract for next season. The Lakers have a plethora of free agents and plenty of questions to answer this summer, from the potential return of LeBron James to a new deal for Austin Reaves, should he decline his player option and become an unrestricted free agent. With Dončić set to begin the first year of his three-year extension, how will the Lakers construct their roster around the league’s top scorer?
pickRows.wayToGo: The Lakers hold only one pick in this year’s draft, No. 25 overall, which they can use to add a young player to develop on a rookie deal, or potentially package in a move to add a more established talent. L.A. can target additional frontcourt help (a pick-and-roll partner with Dončić who can also protect the rim) or perimeter shooting (catch-and-shoot threats ready to take advantage of Dončić’s gravity). Multiple mock drafts have the Lakers pointed toward the frontcourt, with players such as Chris Cenac Jr., Malachi Moreno and Henri Veesaar in this range. — Brian Martin
pickRows.localTeamNotes: Needs a wing who can survive high-leverage minutes. Official NBA.com order pick 25. Need signal: explicit_need_supported_from_single_source; confidence low_medium; usable explicit tags.

The Nuggets dealt with injuries, including Aaron Gordon’s limited availability, and team president and governor Josh Kroenke said running it back with the same core is a strong possibility.

pickRows.seasonSummary: 2025-26 Season: 56-261st Place, Atlantic DivisionLost in first round
pickRows.preDraftOutlook: The Celtics were one of the best teams in the league again, despite parting ways with four of their top eight guys from 2024-25 and playing without Jayson Tatum for the first 62 games. But their streak of four straight trips to the conference semifinals came to an end when they blew a 3-1 lead to the Philadelphia 76ers in the first round. Tatum and Jaylen Brown are both under contract for three more years, but the Celtics need to reconstruct their supporting cast.
pickRows.wayToGo: Brown and Tatum are capable of winning a championship together, so shopping the former isn’t necessary, though maybe there’s a trade out there that can raise the ceiling with a better complement for Tatum. Either way, the Celtics should be on the hunt for frontline depth, either in free agency or with their draft picks. Zuby Ejiofor, Koa Peat or Henri Veesaar could be options late in the first round. — John Schuhmann

pickRows.seasonSummary: 2025-26 Season: 52-302nd place, Central DivisionLost in conference finals
pickRows.preDraftOutlook: A single pick at the end of the first round looks a lot different for a team coming off a trip to the East finals than for one that might have stalled out for the second consecutive spring. That’s how much it meant for the Cavaliers to beat Detroit in Game 7 and advance, landing Donovan Mitchell and the rest in a clash with New York for conference superiority. Cleveland’s title window remains open, which takes some focus off draft options for a high-payroll team more active in the trade market or free agency.
pickRows.wayToGo: The same scouting and draft acumen that landed Tyrese Proctor last year with the No. 49 pick will be tasked with doing even better 20 spots higher this time. Given the Cavs’ fleet of guards, most of the projections at No. 29 are looking at wings and project big men. Arkansas’ Meleek Thomas is a skilled scorer in need of defensive improvement, while Texas wing Dailyn Swain is a scorer still in search of jump-shot consistency. One of the mocks floated Italian center Luigi Suigo, whose decision to join the league next season could swing on getting picked on later than No. 30. — Steve Aschburner

pickRows.preDraftOutlook: In the last 16 months, the Mavs have traded a perennial Kia MVP candidate (Luka Dončić), drafted one of the most heralded prospects in recent memory, traded the future Hall of Famer (Anthony Davis) they got for the first guy, and made major changes in the front office. Cooper Flagg is obviously the foundation, but most of the supporting cast is much older than the Kia Rookie of the Year. That cast includes Kyrie Irving, who should be ready to return at the start of next season, and a new coach after Jason Kidd is out after five seasons.
pickRows.wayToGo: The Mavs fell a spot in the Lottery, but (because of trades) this still could be the highest they pick in the next few years. Flagg is a downhill attacker, so they should be complementing him with as much shooting as they can find. Brayden Burries shot 39% from deep at Arizona, but the Mavs may prefer the potential of Mikel Brown Jr. or the size of Nate Ament. — John Schuhmann

uniqueTeamProfiles.seasonSummary: 2025-26 Season: 17-655th Place, Southeast DivisionDid not qualify for playoffs
uniqueTeamProfiles.preDraftOutlook: After installing new management a year ago, the Wizards went about shuffling the deck in preparation for a reinvention. It’s safe to say that all has gone well. The club made midseason deals to add accomplished veterans in Anthony Davis and Trae Young to a young developmental core. And now the incoming piece from the draft very well could be the building block this franchise has long desired. It’s a new day in D.C.
uniqueTeamProfiles.wayToGo: This draft doesn’t feature a singular, transformational talent like a Victor Wembanyama, but at least two come close enough. And of those, AJ Dybantsa has the size and athletic ability to push him past Darryn Peterson. That’s the safe (and, perhaps,) smart choice for the Wizards, who need to nail this decision for the sake of the future. Dybantsa has the look of greatness and just as important, high entertainment value. — Shaun Powell

uniqueTeamProfiles.seasonSummary: 2025-26 Season: 22-605th place, Northwest DivisionDid not qualify for playoffs
uniqueTeamProfiles.preDraftOutlook: For a team that won 17 games in 2024-25 and 22 games in 2025-26, scoring and depth are necessities. Utah has building blocks with veterans and young players, and next season, the Jazz should be in a position to begin showing more progress.
uniqueTeamProfiles.wayToGo: The Jazz haven’t had a top-two pick since drafting Darrell Griffith second in the 1980 draft. Selecting Kansas guard Darryn Peterson is the kind of scorer and shooter who should accelerate Utah’s rebuild. — Jeff Zillgitt

uniqueTeamProfiles.seasonSummary: 2025-26 Season: 25-575th Place, Southwest DivisionDid not qualify for playoffs
uniqueTeamProfiles.preDraftOutlook: An injury-plagued 2025-26 sent the Grizzlies back down in their recent up-and-down cycle, and this valley might stick if trading Ja Morant comes to fruition. Memphis used 33 different players last season, ranking toward the bottom of both offensive and defensive rankings. Only Cam Spencer (72), Jaylen Wells (69) and Cedric Coward (62) participated in more than 55 games. Morant appeared in just 20, which puts his value at a low point, should Memphis move him.
uniqueTeamProfiles.wayToGo: The first tier of draft elites is four deep, and most mocks pencil in Duke forward Cameron Boozer at No. 3 for the Grizzlies. His fit would be natural alongside center Zach Edey, Wells and Coward, with some NBA pedigree and laudable character traits. At No. 16, Texas Tech guard Christian Anderson could be plugged into Morant’s spot if Memphis deals him — or could play alongside him if he stays. Other backcourt possibilities include Stanford’s Ebuka Okorie and Iowa’s Bennett Stirtz. — Steve Aschburner

uniqueTeamProfiles.seasonSummary: 2025-26 Season: 31-514th place, Central DivisionDid not qualify for playoffs
uniqueTeamProfiles.preDraftOutlook: The resilience, hope, stubbornness, or gullibility of Chicago Bulls fans should never be underestimated when it comes to offseason makeovers. Another disappointing, aimless season finally led to the dismissal of executive VP of basketball operations Arturas Karnisovas and GM Marc Eversley. As much as ownership favored coach Billy Donovan, he resigned and was replaced by former Blazers interim coach Tiago Splitter in June. The Bulls’ streak of three Play-In appearances ended, too. All it took for Chicago to perk up, though, was popping fourth in the draft lottery. The Bulls have another first-round pick, too, fortunate because their talent cupboard is pretty bare.
uniqueTeamProfiles.wayToGo: New basketball boss Bryson Graham will oversee an almost-complete rebuild. He has picks and cap space to fill the roster to match his vision. Chicago is the only team with two picks in the first 15 picks and the No. 4 selection is the obvious prize, with Caleb Wilson or Cameron Boozer slotted in at that spot in many mock drafts. Perimeter shooting and more frontline help are itches to scratch with their remaining picks. — Steve Aschburner

uniqueTeamProfiles.seasonSummary: 2025-26 Season: 42-403rd place, Pacific DivisionLost in SoFi Play-In Tournament
uniqueTeamProfiles.preDraftOutlook: After pulling off one of the greatest in-season turnarounds in NBA history — overcoming a 6-21 start to finish above .500 at 42-40 — the Clippers’ good fortune ran out in the postseason as they were eliminated in the SoFi NBA Play-In Tournament. Then came the NBA Draft Lottery, where the Clippers emerged as one of the biggest winners of the night. With Indiana falling out of the top four, the Clippers acquired their pick (No. 5 overall) as part of the trade that sent Ivica Zubac from LA to Indiana earlier this year.
uniqueTeamProfiles.wayToGo: With the 2026 Draft class bursting with top-tier potential — even beyond the consensus top four of AJ Dybantsa, Darryn Peterson, Cam Boozer, and Caleb Wilson — the Clippers are in a great position to bolster their roster with a potential star. If they look to add a guard to slot in next to Darius Garland, keep an eye on prospects like Brayden Burries, Keaton Wagler and Darius Acuff Jr. — _Brian Martin_

uniqueTeamProfiles.seasonSummary: 2025-26 Season: 20-625th Place, Atlantic DivisionDid not qualify for playoffs
uniqueTeamProfiles.preDraftOutlook: A third straight season with at least 50 losses led to a second straight disappointing result in the 2026 Draft Lottery. The Nets didn’t necessarily strike out in last year’s draft, but none of the five players they selected in the first round was an All-Rookie candidate or a clear future starter on a playoff team. There are some useful veterans on this roster, but no franchise cornerstone.
uniqueTeamProfiles.wayToGo: It seems doubtful, but if there’s any way the Nets can trade into the top four of the Draft, they should go for it, because they need to find a player with the highest ceiling possible. If they remain at six, they’re probably looking at a group of freshmen guards that includes Darius Acuff Jr., Mikel Brown Jr., Brayden Burries and Keaton Wagler. The Nets can also use their cap space for more high-ceiling shopping and asset collection. — John Schuhmann

uniqueTeamProfiles.seasonSummary: 2025-26 Season: 22-605th place, Pacific DivisionDid not qualify for playoffs
uniqueTeamProfiles.preDraftOutlook: With three starters each missing more than half the season — Zach LaVine (39 games played), Domantas Sabonis (19) and Keegan Murray (23) — the Kings posted their lowest win total in 14 years and headed to the Draft Lottery for the 19th time in 20 seasons. Despite entering tied for the fourth-best odds (11.5%) of landing the top pick, the Kings fell all the way to seventh. With the No. 7 pick and a pair of second-round selections, they’ll look for another young building block to pair with last year’s promising rookie trio of Nique Clifford, Maxime Raynaud and Dylan Cardwell.

uniqueTeamProfiles.seasonSummary: 2025-26 Season: 46-361st Place, Southeast DivisionLost in first round
uniqueTeamProfiles.preDraftOutlook: The Hawks are coming off a solid year with a mostly young core which means they’re right on their timeline. Normally they’d be in the market for trading one of their first-round picks for veteran help, but the draft is deep enough that it makes sense to add more youth. The No. 8 pick was famously obtained from the Pelicans on last year’s draft day just to move down a few spots.
uniqueTeamProfiles.wayToGo: The Hawks need size but the depth at guard in the top part of the draft might be too enticing to ignore. With the uncertainty about free agent CJ McCollum, the Hawks could opt to find his replacement. A good choice is Mikel Brown from Louisville, whose best talent might lie with his passing, which would ease that burden from Jalen Johnson. The Hawks also have an additional first-rounder and that’s where a big man could fall, such as Tarris Reed from Connecticut, who’s 6-foot-11 yet raw. — Shaun Powell

uniqueTeamProfiles.seasonSummary: 2025-26 Season: 32-503rd Place, Central DivisionDid not qualify for playoffs
uniqueTeamProfiles.preDraftOutlook: Everything Bucks-related at this stage hangs on the potential trade of superstar Giannis Antetokounmpo. All signs point to him playing his 13th NBA season for another franchise, and if that happens, it seals Milwaukee’s approach to 2026-27 and beyond as a down-to-the-studs rebuild. The roster is threadbare and coach Doc Rivers is gone, having snagged his alleged dream job a couple of seasons too late. Rivers’ replacement, Taylor Jenkins, can fit whether he has Antetokounmpo on board or not.
uniqueTeamProfiles.wayToGo: The Athletic reported that the Bucks met and spoke with a fleet of draft prospects at the Chicago combine, enough that the tactic seemed to extend beyond just the No. 10 pick. It could have been prep work for securing multiple picks in an 11th-hour Antetokounmpo transaction, a way to kick-start the rebuilding process in a draft regarded as deep. One player’s name has appeared in multiple mocks: Tennessee’s Nate Ament. The 6-foot-10 wing could help with or without Antetokounmpo and showed enough between a slow start and a late-season injury to merit consideration here. Another name: Alabama guard Labaron Philon Jr. to team in the backcourt with Ryan Rollins, one of Milwaukee’s few bright spots from last season. — Steve Aschburner

uniqueTeamProfiles.seasonSummary: 2025-26 Season: 37-454th place, Pacific DivisionLost in SoFi Play-In Tournament
uniqueTeamProfiles.preDraftOutlook: Following their third straight appearance in the SoFi NBA Play-In Tournament — a stretch where the Warriors made a run to the conference semifinals in 2025 but missed the playoffs in 2024 and 2026 — the Warriors announced a new two-year deal for head coach Steve Kerr. The extension is a clear indication that Golden State remains in win-now mode around Steph Curry and Draymond Green, rather than looking toward the future. However, the front office enters the offseason facing a slew of potential free agents while two key rotation players — Jimmy Butler III (ACL) and Moses Moody (patella) — are currently dealing with long-term knee injuries.
uniqueTeamProfiles.wayToGo: The Warriors hold a lottery pick, No. 11 overall, for the first time since 2021. That year, they selected Jonathan Kuminga (No. 7) and Moody (No. 14), following the 2020 selection of James Wiseman (No. 2). Those picks represented the franchise’s ill-fated “two timelines” strategy — an attempt to develop elite young talent for the future while remaining a perennial title contender. Now, in 2026, the trio of Curry, Green, and Butler III (assuming a midseason return) are all in their mid-to-late 30s. That raises the question of whether Golden State should use the 11th pick on a young prospect or package it for an established veteran. If the Warriors keep the pick, keep an eye on Yaxel Lendeborg. The 6-foot-9 forward helped lead Michigan to the NCAA title and will turn 24 by the time his rookie NBA season begins. — Brian Martin

uniqueTeamProfiles.seasonSummary: 2025-26 Season: 64-181st place, Northwest DivisionLost in conference finals
uniqueTeamProfiles.preDraftOutlook: The Thunder are in an enviable position given all the talent on the roster, and the front office led by Sam Presti will look to add more talent especially if keeping the current roster becomes problematic financially under salary cap rules. The Thunder prioritize defensive wings, players who can thrive in their player development program and big men who can protect the rim.

uniqueTeamProfiles.seasonSummary: 2025-26 Season: 43-394th Place, Southeast DivisionLost in SoFi Play-In Tournament
uniqueTeamProfiles.preDraftOutlook: Miami will enter the offseason on the hunt for a superstar — that’s the Pat Riley way. And this franchise hasn’t had one since the breakup of the Big 3, with all due respect to Bam Adebayo. That said, the Heat own a good pick in a deep draft, and perhaps their superstar search will fetch a future foundational piece in the first round.
uniqueTeamProfiles.wayToGo: Miami could use depth at guard, a position that will be plentiful even at the No. 13 pick. For example, if Labaron Philon Jr. is around, the Heat would likely not resist. He averaged 22 points at Alabama last year. It’s really about how the first dozen picks impact Miami’s decision-making, because at that spot, there’s the likely chance of a higher-ranking player falling to Miami. — Shaun Powell

uniqueTeamProfiles.seasonSummary: 2025-26 Season: 44-383rd Place, Southeast DivisionLost in SoFi Play-In Tournament
uniqueTeamProfiles.preDraftOutlook: This team was built organically; the Hornets’ top four players — Brandon Miller, LaMelo Ball, Kon Knueppel and Miles Bridges — were obtained through the draft (Bridges in a draft-day trade with the Clippers). And lo and behold, the Hornets have a pair of picks in the top 20. Given that this is a deep draft and that they’ve been rather smart with their draft selections in the past, the Hornets are in a great position to nab another rotational player or two and let the youngsters keep growing together.
uniqueTeamProfiles.wayToGo: The Hornets are marginal at one position — big man. There’s an urgency to spend one of the picks on size, and there should be solid candidates around, notably Hannes Steinbach (6-foot-11) from Washington if Aday Mara (7-foot-3) of Michigan is off the board. Also, with the other pick, 19-year-old wing Karim López comes from the same Australian grooming ground as LaMelo. — Shaun Powell

uniqueTeamProfiles.seasonSummary: 2025-26 Season: 46-363rd Place, Atlantic DivisionLost in first round
uniqueTeamProfiles.preDraftOutlook: The Raptors were one of the league’s most improved teams this season, adding 16 wins to go from the Lottery to the East’s No. 5 seed. They lost in the first round of the playoffs, but Scottie Barnes (25 years old in August) and Collin Murray-Boyles (21) established themselves as franchise cornerstones.
uniqueTeamProfiles.wayToGo: The Raptors need shooting and playmaking, whether they come via trade, free agency or the Draft. But both Barnes and Murray-Boyles are malleable enough that they should be looking to pick the best player available at 19. Christian Anderson and Cameron Carr would give them some much-needed shooting if either is available, but they could also look at potential, long-term replacements for Jakob Poeltl like Chris Cenac Jr., Morez Johnson Jr. or Hannes Steinbach. — John Schuhmann

uniqueTeamProfiles.seasonSummary: 2025-26 Season: 62-201st Place, Southwest DivisionLost in NBA Finals
uniqueTeamProfiles.preDraftOutlook: The Spurs are a modern-day model of team building through the draft, and it helps to be both good at scouting and lucky in the lottery. With the exception of De’Aaron Fox, the top players in the rotation are home grown. Once again, the Spurs — thanks to the Atlanta Hawks — own a top-20 pick, and even though they’re a contending team and should be for years to come with Victor Wembanyama, another highly-regarded young player certainly can’t hurt.
uniqueTeamProfiles.wayToGo: Because of their lofty place in the NBA power pecking order, the Spurs don’t need immediate help. In that sense, it would seem wise for them to take a chance on Jayden Quaintance, the 6-foot-10 forward who only played four games last season for Kentucky while dealing with knee surgery. They can put him in their very respected player development program and watch him grow without any pressure or urgency; he’s just 18 years old. — Shaun Powell

uniqueTeamProfiles.seasonSummary: 2025-26 Season: 60-221st Place, Central DivisionLost in conference semifinals
uniqueTeamProfiles.preDraftOutlook: A marvelous season for Detroit ended with a thud in Game 7 of their Eastern Conference semifinals vs. Cleveland. So much until then had been impressive: Winning 60 games, claiming the East’s No. 1 seed, riding guard Cade Cunningham to Kia MVP contender status, Jalen Duren’s rise to All-Star and All-NBA acclaim, and even bouncing back against Orlando from a 3-1 deficit in the first round. Getting eliminated by the Cavs stung, and the abrupt end of the Pistons’ postseason highlighted some holes to plug, primarily additional scoring and backcourt for Cunningham.
uniqueTeamProfiles.wayToGo: Most of the Pistons’ progress will come from within with the young players such as Duren, Ausar Thompson, and Isaiah Stewart positioned for contract extensions. But the No. 21 pick they got is a legit asset in this deep prospect pool. Duke’s Isaiah Evans could be helpful as a Cunningham sidekick and points source, with shooting range to open up the floor. Three other possibilities: Iowa point guard Bennett Stirtz, Texas Tech guard Christian Anderson and Texas wing Dailyn Swain. — Steve Aschburner

uniqueTeamProfiles.seasonSummary: 2025-26 Season: 45-374th Place, Atlantic DivisionLost in conference semifinals
uniqueTeamProfiles.preDraftOutlook: In VJ Edgecombe and Tyrese Maxey, the Sixers have two star guards who are 20 and 25 years old, respectively. They also have two former Kia MVP candidates — Joel Embiid and Paul George — on the other side of 30. Both have missed many games over the last two years _and_ are owed more than $230 million over the next two years. The Sixers also have a new front office: they fired team president Daryl Morey and replaced him with Mike Gansey shortly after the team was swept in the Eastern Conference semifinals.
uniqueTeamProfiles.wayToGo: Embiid and George probably aren’t going anywhere, but the Gansey-led front office should be all-in on the Maxey-and-Edgecombe timeline. There should be some complementary bigs and big wings to choose from with the No. 22 pick, including Chris Cenac Jr., Isaiah Evans, Allen Graves and Morez Johnson Jr.. — John Schuhmann

uniqueTeamProfiles.seasonSummary: 2025-26 Season: 53-292nd Place, Atlantic Division2026 NBA Champions
uniqueTeamProfiles.preDraftOutlook: The Knicks had some ups and downs in the regular season, but were dominant through the playoffs, going 16-3 through all four rounds to win the team’s first NBA title in 53 years. Their starting lineup remains under contract and they’re built to win now.
uniqueTeamProfiles.wayToGo: While the starters are all under contract, the Knicks’ reserves are mostly free agents. With this being a win-now situation, they should be looking for players that can contribute right away with the 24th and 31st picks, when upperclassmen Joshua Jefferson, Alex Karaban, Bennett Stirtz, Dailyn Swain and Henri Veesaar could be available. — John Schuhmann

uniqueTeamProfiles.seasonSummary: 2025-26 Season: 53-291st place, Pacific DivisionLost in conference semifinals
uniqueTeamProfiles.preDraftOutlook: The Lakers posted back-to-back 50-win seasons for the first time in 15 years, but their 2026 playoff run was doomed by an injury to Luka Dončić and a West Semis matchup with OKC that ended in a sweep. L.A. enters the offseason with only two of its top 10 scorers under contract for next season. The Lakers have a plethora of free agents and plenty of questions to answer this summer, from the potential return of LeBron James to a new deal for Austin Reaves, should he decline his player option and become an unrestricted free agent. With Dončić set to begin the first year of his three-year extension, how will the Lakers construct their roster around the league’s top scorer?
uniqueTeamProfiles.wayToGo: The Lakers hold only one pick in this year’s draft, No. 25 overall, which they can use to add a young player to develop on a rookie deal, or potentially package in a move to add a more established talent. L.A. can target additional frontcourt help (a pick-and-roll partner with Dončić who can also protect the rim) or perimeter shooting (catch-and-shoot threats ready to take advantage of Dončić’s gravity). Multiple mock drafts have the Lakers pointed toward the frontcourt, with players such as Chris Cenac Jr., Malachi Moreno and Henri Veesaar in this range. — Brian Martin

uniqueTeamProfiles.seasonSummary: 2025-26 Season: 54-282nd place, Northwest DivisionLost in first round
uniqueTeamProfiles.preDraftOutlook: The Nuggets are in search of physical, athletic players on all spots on the court with a secondary ballhandler behind Jamal Murray, perimeter scorers and more depth at center behind Nikola Jokic. The Nuggets dealt with injuries, including Aaron Gordon’s limited availability, and team president and governor Josh Kroenke said running it back with the same core is a strong possibility.

uniqueTeamProfiles.seasonSummary: 2025-26 Season: 56-261st Place, Atlantic DivisionLost in first round
uniqueTeamProfiles.preDraftOutlook: The Celtics were one of the best teams in the league again, despite parting ways with four of their top eight guys from 2024-25 and playing without Jayson Tatum for the first 62 games. But their streak of four straight trips to the conference semifinals came to an end when they blew a 3-1 lead to the Philadelphia 76ers in the first round. Tatum and Jaylen Brown are both under contract for three more years, but the Celtics need to reconstruct their supporting cast.
uniqueTeamProfiles.wayToGo: Brown and Tatum are capable of winning a championship together, so shopping the former isn’t necessary, though maybe there’s a trade out there that can raise the ceiling with a better complement for Tatum. Either way, the Celtics should be on the hunt for frontline depth, either in free agency or with their draft picks. Zuby Ejiofor, Koa Peat or Henri Veesaar could be options late in the first round. — John Schuhmann

uniqueTeamProfiles.preDraftOutlook: The Timberwolves will look at point guards or combo guards and centers in the draft – additional help for Anthony Edwards and a big to provide solid minutes when Rudy Gobert is not on the court.
